question: Which of the following acts as the deciding factor in the determination of the valency of an atom?

options.text: Number of electrons in the outermost shell
Number of electrons in the L shell
Number of electrons in the innermost shell
Number of electrons in the K shell

solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of electrons in the outermost shell**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **number of electrons in an atom's outermost shell**, also known **as the valence shell**, is the deciding factor in determining its valency.
 
• **Valency, also known as oxidation number**, is a measure of how many electrons an element can gain, lose, or share when forming chemical compounds.
 
• The** number of valence electrons in an atom determines its valency,** and the valency in turn determines how an element will bond with other elements.
 
• Atoms c**an share, donate, or accept valence electrons with other atoms to form bonds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some key characteristics of a valence electron are:

 
 
• For the main group elements, the valence electron exists only in the outermost electron shell.
 
• A valence electron can exist in the inner shell of a transition metal.
 
• An atom consisting of a closed shell of valence electrons will usually be chemically inert.
 
• A valence electron can either absorb or release energy in the form of a photon.
 
• Valence electrons also determine the electrical conductivity of an element.
